Q1: Britain. A flag with a red cross on white (St George's cross) is on the tower on 4 Aug 1704 (frame 22), then a Union Jack replaces it on the same tower later that day (frames 24-25). The caption "1704 — The Rock changes hands" and a fleet of ships off the town show the handover. From the pictures alone I can't tell who held it before.
Q2: The Great Siege (caption "1779 — The Great Siege", frame 43). Troops and camps appear on the green land north of the Rock, and ships gather offshore (frames 43-51).
Q3: The pictures don't state a reason. The town is shown surrounded by land camps and by ships on the sea, and in Apr 1781 fires and damage appear in the town (frames 61-65). I would guess it is cut off by the siege, with no supplies getting in, but the frames never show hunger or food directly. Not sure.
Q4: Ships. A group of ships sails in toward the town in Oct 1780 and Apr 1781 (frames 58, 59-61). They look like a relief fleet, but the pictures don't confirm what they carry.
Q5: A sea battle at night on 13-14 Sep 1782. A line of ships is shown burning and smoking beside the Rock (frames 86-88; also frames 6-7, which jump ahead to the same date). Before that, a line of floating batteries forms up on 11-13 Sep (frames 76-85). I can't tell which side the burning ships belong to.
Q6: The flat sandy land is empty grass and fields with lines of trenches and walls through the 1700s and 1800s. Small buildings start to appear around 1904-1910 (frames 109-117). Then come camps and buildings in 1939 (captioned "A runway on the sand", frames 118-123) and a runway in 1939-46 (frame 146). Later it fills with housing, roads, a car park and a big built-up area by 2015-2026.
Q7: In Jun-Aug 1969 something happens at the gate: a wall or fence is drawn across the land in front of the Rock, near the town (frames 147-149), and no people are shown. The border looks closed from then on. By 1973-1984 the scene hasn't clearly changed (frames 150-151) and no reopening is shown, so I'm not sure what happens later.
Q8: The pictures don't show one thing that clearly links them. The two towns sit side by side across the flat land: the Rock's town on one side and a large Spanish-looking city on the other, in 2026. A runway or airfield, roads, a car park and houses fill the land between them (frames 155-173). People walk through a narrow street in 2026 (frames 158-159). So the link is probably people, roads and the shared land. Not sure.

Floating batteries are shown, but the sea battle in Sep 1782 isn't clearly explained or its result shown.
The street scene from 1910 has no context.
